newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - JULY 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - JULY 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- Pakistani government is likely to scrap three private power projects and carry out further review of nine projects.
- Five sisters were killed and three other family members were seriously injured in Lahore when the rooftop of their house collapsed after recent rains.
- The government has withdrawn sales tax on text books.
THE NATION
- Former commerce minister Ahmed Mukhtar said the new trade policy will increase trade imbalance between India and Pakistan.
DAWN

- Talks with the visiting International Monetary Fund mission are quite encouraging and will hopefully lead to the signing of a new $1.5 billion loan in October this year, said Planning Commission's deputy chairman Hafeez Pasha.
- The government has imposed a complete ban on new employments and adopted other cost-saving measures as part of austerity drive.
- Pakistan and Italy signed an agreement for promoting and protecting bilateral investment and enhancing economic ties.
- A Turkish holding company has sought the assistance of a private Pakistani investment bank for setting up of the company's subsidiary in Pakistan.
- The proposed shipping policy, the draft of which is ready to be tabled before the parliament, declares shipping as an industry and recommends fiscal incentives to give it a boost.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Privatisation Commission has selected four units of Ghee Corporation of Pakistan for sale early next month.
- The Corporate Law Commission has completed review of Monopoly Control Law to make it effective and efficient, said Commission's chairman Shafiur Rehman.
- Mobil is stepping up its business in Pakistan with an extensive range of lubricants.
FINANCIAL POST
- The Muslim Commercial Bank has offered voluntary retirement to its staff members.

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz has said the government was working on a plan to further reduce the prices of fertilisers and other farm inputs to supplement the incentive package for the agriculture sector.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
